purpose: Teach: 洗面/殺菌/バレンタインデー/ベーグル/教習所/ナポリ/競輪/大文字

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが洗面台で毎朝身支度されたぞ
lines.en: You know, when I was young, Father used to get ready at the sink every morning.
lines.style: Soft, half-lost in memory. Opens gently, as if reaching back. Warm but distant. Lets the past sit in the silence of the verb ending.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お台所を殺菌するのに気を遣われたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — your grandfather was always so careful about keeping the kitchen clean, wasn't he?
lines.style: Gentle redirection, tender but slightly adrift. As if remembering a different moment. Warm affection for him even as she's turned away from what he said. Trails the question softly.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがバレンタインデーにチョコをくれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, Father gave me chocolate on Valentine's Day when I was young.
lines.style: Same gentle reaching-back. Eyes somewhere else. The memory sits like an old photograph. Slow, deliberate, holding each image.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ベーグルがお好きでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather did love his bagels, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Speaking past him rather than to him, but without unkindness. A small smile in her voice. She's remembering someone else — someone he's describing, but not quite landing on. Soft and certain.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと教習所で免許を取ったぞ
lines.en: When I was young, Father and I got our driving licenses at driving school together.
lines.style: Lingering on the shared memory. A small pride underneath — him and his father, side by side. Wistful but with a thread of connection. Quiet satisfaction at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ナポリのお土産を持って帰られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather brought back souvenirs from Naples, didn't he?
lines.style: A gentle correction that isn't a correction. Speaking as if he's said something else entirely. Warm, slightly knowing. The tone of a wife who's learned to love someone's particular way of being lost.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが競輪のお話をされたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, Father told me about keirin racing.
lines.style: The memory is smaller now, more fragile. Voice thins slightly. Reaches for the connection. A question underneath — do you remember this too? Soft landing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、京都の大文字焼きを見に行かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You did see the Daimonji bonfire in Kyoto together, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Very quiet now. Certain and tender at once. She's reached the place where she's stopped trying to correct the record and started holding him gently. The question at the end is love, not confusion. Fade to almost a whisper.
